errors.english: it is shown that the recipient actually accepts and takes possession of the offering
errors.why: rjes su 'dzin pa here is anugraha: the word shows the recipient's favour or gratification toward the giver, not physical taking possession.

note: A close, readable rendering of a word-by-word jātaka commentary; inline glosses (Vedic deities, nature spirits) are padding but harmless.

errors.english: which possess the nature of arising and ceasing
errors.why: The Sautrāntika formations are described as having arising and ceasing AND being free from the faults of permanence and annihilation; the second qualifier is dropped.

note: Accurate account of the Sautrāntika position and Bhāviveka's reply, with the MMK verse and the two inferences correctly rendered.
Faithful rendering of the Abhidharma account of the three calamities, the twenty intermediate eons and the eighty-eon great eon.

errors.english: This belongs to the Victorious One [note: Sanskrit: Jayanta, referring to the philosopher or a cited master].
errors.why: rGyal ba can is the proper name Jina, the earlier commentator on the Pramāṇavārttikālaṃkāra whose interpretation is being reported, not the Buddha and not Jayanta.

fix.find: This belongs to the Victorious One [note: Sanskrit: Jayanta, referring to the philosopher or a cited master].

errors.english: The phrase "actor" or "jester" indicates one who engages
errors.why: dzab mkhan is a japa-maker, one who mutters recitations, who speaks even with no listener; not an actor or jester.
The sentence continues on the next side (the statement is an example of the parity of treatise and one's own words); nothing says the treatise is refuted.

note: The argument on treatise and own-word invalidation is followed in outline, but a commentator's name is turned into the Buddha with a wrong gloss and a key example word is mistranslated.

errors.english: Through realization they are made to appear mixed.
errors.why: In this Dharmakīrtian context it is conceptual cognition (vikalpa) that mixes distinct own-natures, not realization.

note: Dense Pramāṇa commentary on conventional validity rendered with reasonable accuracy; some sentences are loose but the argument is preserved.

errors.english: how could the intellect of women who conquer men apply to those possessed of such glory?
errors.why: The verse (strījitānāṃ matiḥ kutaḥ) asks where the intelligence is of men conquered by women, men of fortune who bow to them; it condemns the deluded, it does not praise them.

fix.find: how could the intellect of women who conquer men apply to those possessed of such glory?
fix.replace: where is the intelligence of those who, though possessed of fortune, bow down and are conquered by women?

errors.english: whose minds are intoxicated with supreme bliss
errors.why: Sanskrit svasukhakṣībacetasām: minds drunk on their own pleasure, a censure, not spiritual bliss.

errors.english: Having committed that sin in previous lives
errors.why: spyad = bhuktvā: having experienced (suffered the fruit of) that sin in previous births, of which a remainder still marks him.

fix.find: Having committed that sin in previous lives
fix.replace: Having experienced the fruit of that sin in previous lives

note: The narrative verses are mostly right, but the didactic verse on men ruled by women is inverted into praise and the karmic point is misrendered.

errors.why: 'du ba in this anti-ātman debate is samavāya, inherence (of cognition in the self), not aggregation.

errors.english: To demonstrate that in the distinct states of remembering and experiencing, there is no separate rememberer
errors.why: The point is that for that (self) which is distinct from memory and experience there is no being-the-rememberer etc., not that remembering and experiencing are distinct states.

note: Good grasp of the memory-and-self argument overall; a couple of clauses are misconstrued.
Faithful glossary-style rendering of the arhat epithets, the three vidyās, abhijñās and four pratisaṃvids.

errors.english: spoken for the purpose of guiding beings
errors.why: drang ba'i don is neyārtha: the Blessed One taught the three vehicles as a teaching of provisional meaning, a key hermeneutical claim lost here.

fix.find: spoken for the purpose of guiding beings
fix.replace: spoken as a teaching of provisional meaning (neyārtha)
